claims: NASA's Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch no earlier than 6:24 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
NASA's Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B.
Artemis II mission is a 10-day mission.
Artemis II mission will be the first crewed flight of the SLS rocket.
Artemis II mission will be the first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft.
Artemis II mission will send four astronauts on a flyby around the Moon.
Target launch time for Artemis II is April 1, 2026, 6:24 p.m. EDT.
Launch window for Artemis II is two hours from 6:24 p.m. EDT to 8:24 p.m. EDT.
Five additional launch attempts for Artemis II are available through April 6 if needed.
Crew of Artemis II includes NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
Artemis II is a test flight to verify Orion’s life-support systems with a crew in deep space.
Final countdown for Artemis II began on Monday, March 30, at 4:44 p.m. EDT.
As of March 31, weather forecasts for Artemis II launch are 80% favorable.
SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft are currently on the pad at Launch Pad 39B
NASA's YouTube Channel will stream the Artemis II launch.
Coverage on NASA's YouTube Channel for Artemis II launch starts at 7:45 a.m. for fueling operations.
Spaceflight Now will provide live updates throughout the day for Artemis II launch.
Public viewing is available for Artemis II launch
